_note: CWE, NIST 800-53/800-61 and PCI DSS references below are real published control/weakness IDs used for mapping context. CVE examples are REAL historical CVEs cited for illustration, not detected live against a live feed. PECA 2016 is Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act -- a LEGAL statute, not a technical control framework, so it is mapped at the legal-obligation level rather than a control ID.

T1486.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
cwe: CWE-664: Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime
example_cves: CVE-2021-34527 (PrintNightmare, used in multiple ransomware intrusions)
CVE-2023-3519 (Citrix NetScaler, chained into ransomware initial access)
pci_dss_v4: Requirement 5: Protect systems and networks from malicious software

T1490.name: Inhibit System Recovery

pci_dss_v4: Requirement 10: Log and monitor all access to system components and cardholder data
peca_2016: Section 7: Unauthorized interference with critical infrastructure information system or data

firewall_fade_dataset._note: No single network dataset is universally published under the exact name 'FADE'. This project uses a FADE-style schema (Flow-based Anomaly DEtection) consistent with common flow-based IDS datasets (e.g. CICIDS-style 5-tuple + statistical flow features). Synthetic data, generated for this project -- replace with your actual FADE dataset source if you have one.

framework_reference.CWE: Common Weakness Enumeration - MITRE's catalog of software/hardware weakness types.
framework_reference.CVE: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures - MITRE/NVD catalog of specific disclosed vulnerabilities.
framework_reference.NIST_800_53: NIST Special Publication 800-53 - security and privacy controls for federal information systems.
framework_reference.NIST_800_61: NIST SP 800-61 - Computer Security Incident Handling Guide (the Prep/Detect/Contain/Eradicate/Recover lifecycle used in this project's incident flow).
framework_reference.PCI_DSS_v4: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.0 - 12 top-level requirements for entities handling cardholder data.
framework_reference.PECA_2016: Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 - the controlling cybercrime statute for incidents on Pakistani infrastructure; a legal, not technical, framework.
